solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Noise is not good at the outset at table?

parts.note: a din is a loud racket

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its opening letter, so only the starts of these words are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of three consecutive words

explanation.surface: A complaint that a dinner gathering starts off far too loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the outset' looks like it modifies only 'good', but it takes the starts of all three words before it. The question mark flags a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seated at table for a meal is in the middle of eating dinner, so the participle fits.

clue.text: Dignitary in Paris is in charge of Home

parts.note: Dom is a title of honour for some monks and Portuguese nobles
est is French for 'is'
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A French official who runs the Home Office, or the equivalent ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' tells you to translate the next word into French, so 'is' becomes EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Home as an adjective, as in home affairs or home policy, means internal to a country or household.

clue.text: Arrivals from France — usual standard, all new, staying principally

parts.note: a norm is the usual standard

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so each word contributes just its leading letter

parts.note: the leading letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Immigrants from France meet the usual standard, and every newcomer stays.
explanation.walkthrough: The Normans came from Normandy in northern France and conquered England in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans were the invaders from northern France who arrived in England with William the Conqueror.

clue.text: Very much ungoverned, regularly missing

indicators.note: losing letters at a steady interval leaves every other one behind

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A lawless place where order is very much absent at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the odd-numbered letters of the long word and the even ones remain.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British phrase, as in 'it pleased him no end', means enormously or to a great degree.

clue.text: Bye! One boorish fellow arrested in public transport, drinking too much

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a bye
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: someone arrested is held, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: a bus is public transport
a loose clipping of lout, a boorish fellow

explanation.surface: Waving goodbye as a drunken yob is hauled off a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored without the bat touching the ball, written B. The boorish fellow is best read as LOUT trimmed to LOU, which the setter leaves unsignalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Bibulous is a formal adjective for someone fond of alcohol and inclined to overindulge.

clue.text: Unlucky Bianca periodically distrustful, losing head

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, here every other one of the name

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Bianca

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: distrustful means suspicious

explanation.surface: Bianca, unlucky in love, has become periodically distrustful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' takes the even letters of Bianca, INA; 'losing head' drops the S from SUSPICIOUS, leaving USPICIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inauspicious means showing bad omens, so an inauspicious start is an unlucky one.

clue.text: Foreign articles — I don't know the way to go

parts.note: UN is French for 'a' and DER is German for 'the'
a quiz contestant says 'pass' when stumped

explanation.surface: A puzzled traveller abroad admits not knowing which route to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The way to go' reads as advice, but it is a literal route, a passage running beneath a road.
explanation.definitionFit: An underpass is a tunnel or road beneath another road, literally a route people travel along.

clue.text: Natural old doctor — caring

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth, kindly old-fashioned family doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun paired with 'old', but it is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic food and materials are produced without artificial chemicals, so the word is a synonym for natural.

clue.text: Smaller group with name for bishop's daily event

indicators.note: with name for bishop, one letter stands in place of the other in the word

parts.note: a subset is a smaller group drawn from a larger one
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A small group gathers with a bishop for his daily routine.
explanation.walkthrough: In SUBSET, 'name for bishop' puts N where the B was.
explanation.definitionFit: The going down of the sun happens every evening, an occurrence that comes round each day.

clue.text: Very involved in horse trial ultimately quite something

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: Taking part in a horse trial turns out to be quite an experience.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside MARE, and the last letter of 'trial' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel is a wonder, an impressive person or thing, which is what calling it quite something says.

clue.text: Top dog

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted garment for the upper body
second meaning: a breed of Welsh corgi named after a county in Wales

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top dog' is the phrase for a winner, but the two words are separate definitions. The Cardigan is one of the two breeds of Welsh corgi.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a buttoned knitted jumper worn on the upper body and a corgi breed from Cardiganshire in Wales.

clue.text: Competitor as tie-in film's prepared

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up from its ingredients, so these letters are put together anew

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: A contender being readied for a film tie-in deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S of 'film's' supplies a letter; the rest of the surface is pure fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A semifinalist is a player or team still contending in the round before the final, so a competitor.

clue.text: Course stewards on move about noon

indicators.note: to be about something is to go around it, surrounding it
things on the move shift position, so these letters change order

parts.note: taken as written
N stands for noon, the n in a.m. and p.m. notation

explanation.surface: Officials at a golf course bustling about at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: St Andrews in Scotland is the home of golf, and its Old Course is the most famous in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: St Andrews is the Scottish town whose Old Course is a celebrated golf links, so it is an example of a course.

clue.text: Limits of solid fuel stove

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the extent or bounds of something
second meaning: a large kitchen cooker

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' links the two meanings while making them read as one phrase about a stove's limits.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the span between upper and lower bounds and a large kitchen cooker such as an Aga.

clue.text: At home Leo maybe providing one opportunity (not hard) — nothing much

parts.note: in means at home
Leo is an example of a star sign of the zodiac
providing means if, as in 'providing it rains'
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: not hard tells us the letter for hard is left out of the word

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A Leo at home, given a single chance, achieves little of note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not hard' removes H from CHANCE, leaving CANCE to finish the chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignificance is unimportance, the quality of amounting to very little.

clue.text: Somewhat evoking Arden in growth, this maybe?

definitions.text: Somewhat evoking Arden in growth, this maybe?

indicators.note: somewhat means only a part, so the answer is a stretch of the text that follows

parts.note: the letters span four words

explanation.surface: Tending plants might call to mind Shakespeare's Forest of Arden.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'evokinG ARDEN IN Growth'. The whole clue also describes the answer, since cultivating growth evokes the Forest of Arden in As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardening is the cultivation of plants, a pursuit of encouraging growth that might suggest a leafy pastoral setting.

clue.text: Popular release as alternative to Biro, say

parts.note: something in is fashionable
to vent is to let out
or offers an alternative

explanation.surface: A newly launched pen, popular as a replacement for the Biro.
explanation.walkthrough: Biro looks like the pen brand, but it is László Bíró, the Hungarian who created the ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: László Bíró devised the ballpoint pen, so he is an example of someone who came up with a new device.

clue.text: Ate in parish inn possibly as this is outside — plain feature mainly?

definitions.text: this is outside — plain feature mainly?

indicators.note: 'possibly' allows another arrangement, so these letters may be shuffled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Diners eat in a village pub while the weather stays outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the line 'The rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain' from My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather is outdoors, and the song lyric says this Iberian downpour falls mostly on flat lowland, making it a feature of the plain.

clue.text: Bash in lively haunt — this one?

definitions.text: Bash in lively haunt — this one?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
lively means animated, so these letters move about

parts.note: taken as written
a bash is a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: A party at a lively local spot, perhaps exactly this sort of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' suggests a party, but it means a try, as in 'have a bash'. The whole clue also describes the answer: a lively haunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangout is a place someone frequents, a regular haunt where a party might happen.

clue.text: Contrary to assumptions at first, profits over time

indicators.note: at first points to the beginning, so only the leading letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
gains are profits
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Earnings defied what was expected at the start and grew steadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over time' sounds like a phrase, but T stands alone after the profits.
explanation.definitionFit: Against means in opposition to, as does the preposition phrase contrary to.

clue.text: Music — leave session, the last to depart

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: the final letter of the word departs, so it is dropped

parts.note: a spell is a session or period of time

explanation.surface: A musician leaves the recording session, the last one out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'leave session' as one action, but leave is its own piece, a verb meaning go; 'the last to depart' trims the session word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel is a style of Christian religious song from African American churches.

clue.text: Resilience as British leave? Small amount

indicators.note: when something leaves, it is taken away and no longer there

parts.note: bounce is the ability to recover quickly
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A wry question about how much fortitude Britain showed on departing the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British leave' calls up Brexit, but 'leave' is a verb telling the B to go from BOUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, and figuratively a tiny quantity, as in 'not an ounce of sense'.

clue.text: Initially guess a mum's age — silly, like this

definitions.text: Initially guess a mum's age — silly, like this

indicators.note: something silly is muddled and nonsensical, so these letters are jumbled
initially means at the start, so just the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trying to guess your mother's age is a foolish undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: guessing a woman's age is a classic no-win pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug's game is British slang for a foolish or futile activity, a mug being a gullible person.

clue.text: Ray's part of task at exercises

indicators.note: part of means only a portion, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across three words

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray has a role in a workout routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray looks like a man's name, but it is the flat fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A skate is a type of flat cartilaginous fish belonging to the ray family.

clue.text: Fruitful crop Filipino not half cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated suggests working the ground over, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only half of the word is wanted, so its second four letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Filipino farmer grows a crop that yields well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' cuts FILIPINO to FILI; with CROP, those letters are rearranged as 'cultivated' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolific means producing abundantly, as a fruitful tree yields plenty.

clue.text: Publication, final, that's attractive

parts.note: short for magazine
net means final, as in the amount after deductions

explanation.surface: The last issue of a glossy publication is an appealing one.
explanation.walkthrough: Net here is the figure after all deductions, as in net profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet draws iron towards it, and figuratively draws people, so it is something that attracts.

clue.text: Excellent, I entrance Sue!

parts.note: lit is modern slang for excellent
taken as written
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone praising themselves for enchanting a woman named Sue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads as the verb meaning enchant, and Sue as a name; both are other parts of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to bring a legal action against someone, which is what taking a case to court involves.

clue.text: Gambler on the mend

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who places wagers
second meaning: recovering from an illness

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a punter whose fortunes are recovering; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a person who places wagers and an adjective for someone recovering their health.
